correctness.rationale: For arbitrary independent conductance variables the Kirchhoff index is a strictly convex inverse-Laplacian trace under connected support. This enforces classwise symmetric weights, not merely an ansatz. Direct cut-vertex resistance addition gives K=sum[(N-m)/x+N(m-1)/(x+my)]. The scalar shape derivative has a unique minimizer and an exact endpoint inequality at Q/P=2N/M; the inequality A+C=mM is checked. Cauchy–Schwarz gives a sharp globally unique budget split and exact value. Exact grounded-inverse calculations and phase/KKT checks passed 480 assertions; they supplement an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General convex optimization and marginal KKT conditions establish existence and necessary/sufficient inequalities, not the closed heterogeneous optimizer. The full theorem is not a corollary of the equal-blade formula by parameter substitution because differing blade sizes and price classes break blade-transitivity, permit any mixture of edge supports and require an additional global budget coupling.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new statement strictly contains acknowledged special cases; those special cases alone neither imply the heterogeneous minimizer nor the arbitrary mixed-support realization. Combining published general principles with the new blockwise scalar and budget equality calculations yields the result, but no inspected publication gives the resulting complete formula or independent price-phase law. Claim is confined to exactly that additional theorem, without re-claiming the antecedent pieces.

originality.rationale: The inspected general convex-design, block-Kirchhoff and power-cost literature provides separate ingredients but no stated all-dimensional, per-blade heterogeneous optimum with arbitrary mixed peripheral-edge support and the exact coupled spending formula. A previously established equal-size/common-price windmill theorem and a published single-triangle price threshold cover special cases and are expressly not the assessed novel contribution. The novel statement concerns the full family of differently sized blades with independently variable price pairs; residual historical equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A 2024 specialist windmill-index paper was accessible only as an abstract; although its described objective is unweighted index calculation, its full contents were not compared.
An unindexed graph-design note may state an equivalent heterogeneous support/budget formula; a negative search is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The independently selectable presence or absence of every differently priced clique interior and the universal threshold depending on total peripheral count make a complete, implementable resource-design classification. The coupled square-root global spending formula is needed when blade sizes and prices vary and is not supplied by the existing common-price equal-size special case. This is a natural heterogeneous block-network problem rather than a fixed arbitrary-size numerical slice.
